differential.name: Non‑alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD)
differential.rationale: Mild ALT>AST in a diabetic, hypertensive patient with metabolic syndrome suggests steatosis.

differential.name: Alcoholic liver disease
differential.rationale: Unhealthy alcohol use can cause a modest transaminase rise, though AST/ALT ratio is not classic.

differential.name: Statin‑induced hepatotoxicity
differential.rationale: Dyslipidemia likely treated with statins; these can cause mild isolated ALT elevations.

differential.name: Chronic viral hepatitis (e.g., hepatitis C)
differential.rationale: Possible cause of persistent low‑grade transaminitis, though no specific risk factors noted.

differential.name: Hereditary hemochromatosis
differential.rationale: Can present with mild ALT elevation; less likely given age and lack of iron studies.
